name: Dodge Charger R/T / Scat Pack
reliability: 7/10 — simple, robust HEMI V8s, but the MDS lifter tick can escalate to cam damage
cost_to_own: Insurance: High (V8 muscle) · Maintenance ~$650/yr (premium fuel, thirsty)
popular_mods: Cold air intake + 87/93-octane PCM tune (DiabloSport / HP Tuners)
Lowering springs, sway bars, drag radials
Upgraded lifters/cam or MDS delete on a rebuild
oil_interval: Every 5,000-6,000 miles (don't stretch — sludge starves the MDS lifters)

generations.LX (2006–2010): Modern Charger revived as a 4-door muscle sedan. SRT8 ran a 6.1L HEMI. RWD or AWD.
generations.LD (2011–2023): Refreshed platform. R/T (5.7), Scat Pack (6.4/392), SRT Hellcat (6.2 supercharged, 707-717hp). The last of the HEMI Chargers.
generations.LB Daytona (2024–present): All-new — electric Charger Daytona plus twin-turbo inline-6 'Hurricane' SIXPACK versions replacing the HEMI. Now offered as a 2-door and 4-door.

common_issues: HEMI MDS lifter tick → collapsed lifters and camshaft damage if ignored
Exhaust manifold bolt breakage (exhaust tick on cold start)
Thirsty — real-world fuel economy is low
Heavy curb weight blunts agility versus lighter rivals
maintenance_tips: Change oil every 5-6k with the correct spec to keep MDS oil passages clean
Address any lifter tick immediately before it wipes the camshaft
Inspect/replace exhaust manifold bolts if you hear a cold-start tick
Run premium fuel in the 392/Scat Pack

engine.detail: 6.4L 392 HEMI V8 making 485 hp and 475 lb-ft in the Scat Pack; the R/T runs the 5.7L HEMI (395 lb-ft). Simple, robust pushrod V8s with cylinder-deactivating MDS.
engine.watch: The MDS lifter tick is the notorious failure — if ignored it escalates to a collapsed lifter and a wiped camshaft, so address any tick immediately; broken exhaust manifold bolts also cause a distinctive cold-start tick.

drivetrain.detail: Rear-wheel drive through the stout 8-speed TorqueFlite automatic (ZF-based 8HP).
drivetrain.watch: The transmission is generally robust and trouble-free; keep up with fluid service on hard-launched or tuned cars.

suspension.detail: Independent front and multilink rear under a big four-door unibody muscle sedan.
suspension.watch: A ~4,360 lb curb weight blunts agility next to lighter rivals — it is a straight-line bruiser first; lowering springs and sway bars are the common handling fix.

brakes.detail: Large ventilated discs, with four-piston Brembo front calipers standard on the Scat Pack.
brakes.watch: There is a lot of mass to haul down — fresh pads and fluid matter, and the brakes work hard on a heavy car driven hard.

fuel.detail: Naturally aspirated, port-injected V8 that wants premium fuel in the 392/Scat Pack.
fuel.watch: Genuinely thirsty — real-world economy is low (~15 city mpg) — and do not stretch oil changes: sludge starves the MDS oil passages that feed the lifters.

body.detail: A big, heavy full-size four-door unibody — real muscle-sedan practicality, and the LD car is the last of the HEMI Chargers before the electric/Hurricane LB.
body.watch: Solid, simple structure; the curb weight is the defining trade-off for the four-door usability.
